concept.name: Trendline
concept.definition: A straight line drawn on a chart connecting two or more price points and extended forward, used to visualize a trend and to act as a dynamic reference for support (up trendline, connecting rising lows) or resistance (down trendline, connecting falling highs). It is a discretionary drawing tool, not an objective market feature.
concept.intuition: Connect the dots of the trend's pullbacks, and the resulting line sketches the trend's natural floor (or ceiling).
concept.mechanics: An up trendline connects two or more ascending lows (the second low must exceed the first); a down trendline connects two or more descending highs. More touches without a break are taken as evidence of significance; a close beyond the line is a warning that the trend may be changing, to be confirmed by other evidence.
concept.failure_modes: Placement is subjective — different analysts draw different lines on the same chart; trendline breaks generate frequent false warnings, especially on steep or shallow trends.
concept.misconceptions: That a trendline break proves the trend has reversed; Fidelity itself cautions it should serve only as a warning requiring confirmation.
concept.example: Connecting the pullback lows at 50, 52, and 54 in a rising stock yields an up trendline; price bouncing off the line a fourth time is read as the uptrend remaining intact.
